extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (applicants, grantees, institutional administrators, and NIH staff)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models (NAMs and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches, including New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), to enhance human relevance and translational potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on choosing scientifically sound approaches that best answer the research question; NIH encourages models that increase human relevance and translational potential while reminding investigators to select the model appropriate to the question rather than adopting methods for novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: New Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure has key features and an application format; applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the 6-minute NIH overview to learn key features and correct application formatting. Be aware that, after peer review and before JIT, applications can be split into linked awards—plan proposals and budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available, based on a simplified set of required elements for preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans, use the 2026 pilot format and include the required simplified elements; consult the resource for exact required items and formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative encourage embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research, and provide reminders for applications and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should incorporate plans or elements that promote replication and reproducibility where appropriate, consider highlighted topics related to replication in their proposals, and follow NIH guidance to demonstrate how their work supports reliable, reproducible science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving this designation should understand it reflects placement in the middle third of applications (not discussed at full meeting) and consider follow-up resources or clarifications from NIH about implications for resubmission or next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review (CSR consolidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review has been centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of process changes resulting from centralization (e.g., potential differences in study section handling, timelines, or administrative practices) and consult CSR guidance or notices for details that may affect submission and review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Small Business/Seed Fund program availability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Seed Fund and small business program are active resources for innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business applicants should monitor NIH announcements about available programs, eligibility, and application procedures for the Seed Fund and other small-business-focused funding opportunities.
